ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, managers and authorized signatories against EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, United Kingdom HMT sanctions, and Luxembourg domestic restrictive measures. Politically Exposed Persons are identified through international PEP databases and domestic sources. Enhanced due diligence, independent verification of source of funds, adverse media screening and ongoing transaction monitoring are required in accordance with the Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation No 12-02. Findings are documented and retained for a minimum of five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be recorded in the RCS using the Latin alphabet. The statutes may be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish, and French is the standard administrative language. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script for RCS registration. The legal entity name must contain the suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' and must not create confusion with any existing Luxembourg company or trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected by the RCS/LBR, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Luxembourg Business Registers Registrar within one month of the rejection notice. If the rejection is confirmed, a formal administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg Tribunal Administratif within three months of the confirmation decision. The appeal must be introduced by a Luxembourg-qualified lawyer, and alternative name reservations may be submitted in parallel to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office-only solution is not permissible for the planned manufacturing of surgical suture needles. Luxembourg company law requires a registered office in Luxembourg, and commercial substance doctrine requires physical premises, local management, operational staff, equipment and records. For ISIC 3250 medical device manufacturing, the Ministry of Health and the competent labour inspectorate require an actual production site in Luxembourg. A registered-agent address may support administrative filings only and cannot replace the physical manufacturing and storage premises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Estimated probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Luxembourg Ministry of Health, the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines) and municipal authorities within the first twelve months of commencement is approximately 80%. Pre-licensing site verification is mandatory before manufacturing approval.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended), Articles 1, 43-71 (SARL provisions), and 980-1 et seq. (electronic incorporation); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Statuts) and Certificate of Incorporation (Acte de Constitution)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,394.00 minimum share capital, fully subscribed; at least 50% (EUR 6,197.00) paid up in cash before incorporation, held on a blocked escrow account in the name of the SARL in formation with a duly licensed credit institution, and released to the legal representatives upon RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a statutory auditor's report and are fully paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator(s) hereby subscribe to the 12,000 qualifying shares of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL) in formation, each sharing equally in profits, and that the total subscribed capital shall not be less than EUR 12,394.00, with the statutory minimum to be paid into the blocked escrow account prior to signature of the notarial deed. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the company shall be established at [Registered Office Address], Luxembourg, and that management may rent or otherwise secure such premises. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] and [Name] are appointed as managers (Gérants), each with sole signature authority acting individually, and that the managers shall be and hereby are authorized to file the Articles of Association with the Trade and Companies Register and complete all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Certification of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Notaire) with corporate law practice.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French or German; provide to the notary for verification of legal capacity of incorporators, capital subscription, and the registry of blocked bank account. The notary certifies the deed of constitution and sends certified copy to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate of release (Dépôt de fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal capacity or capital deficiencies, the articles are amended and re-notarized; capital discontinuities are corrected through re-payment into escrow.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg bank or credit institution subject to CSSF supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the company's name 'SARL en formation'; transfer EUR 12,394 minimum, confirming the paid-in share of at least EUR 6,197. Request a blocked-funds certificate (Attestation de dépôt) naming the notary and company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank KYC rejects, update economic substance documentation and resubmit; choose an alternative CSSF-regulated bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Deed Signature and RCS Registration Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers e-slot
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notary signs the deed; file legalized copy and statutory declarations through the RCS e-form. Pay RCS filing fee (EUR 19). The RCS issues the registration number and certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation (Acte de constitution)
Managers' declarations of social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, within 15 days correct and refile; if name conflict, submit three alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Corporate Income Tax and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, apply for the national tax number (TVA number) using form 010C and for social security employer registration for employees. This is a one-window online application via MyGuichet.
required_dossiers: Lease or deed to registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax form incomplete, revise; register for social security through the CCSS portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Gazette and Post-Incorporation Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mémorial C (Official Registry) via RCS official announcements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the notarized deed is published in the Recueil des Sociétés et Associations (RSA); update the register with the statutory publication reference; finalize bank account activation for operational transactions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, obtain a certificate of pending publication from the notary.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé) – Division of Pharmacy and Medicines, in coordination with the Medical Devices Department; and the Ministry of the Economy for industrial establishment.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturing Authorization for Medical Devices (Autorisation de fabrication de dispositifs médicaux) under Luxembourg Law of 4 July 2014 on medical devices, transposing MDD 93/42/EEC / MDR (EU) 2017/745

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Registration (Sector 43 of the environmental register), requiring an environmental permit for wastewater discharge, ventilation emissions, and biohazard waste management; a full EIA is not required if annual production below Annex I thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater pH 6.0-9.0, COD ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L; VOC concentration ≤ 20 mg/m³ for sterile wiping and solvent use; all liquid and solid biohazard waste must be autoclaved or incinerated per EU waste code 18 01 03.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Inspection Générale de la Police Grand-Ducale – Department of Civil Defense; structural load inspection for cleanroom and sterilization equipment; occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) on ventilation, noise, and ergonomic compliance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct income taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for value added tax; business registration via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) at www.lbr.lu; taxpayer portal: www.guichet.lu and www.myguichet.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment, VAT registration is made electronically through MyGuichet or by filing Form 1, Déclaration d'assujettissement à la TVA, with the AEDT. EU-established taxable persons may register directly; non-EU-established persons generally must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative, sign a joint mandate with the AEDT, and provide corporate constitutive documents, proof of original foreign VAT ID, and business licences. The AEDT in turn issues a Luxembourg VAT number (TVA LU), which becomes the VAT ID for electronic invoicing, export refund claims and Intrastat declarations. Income tax TIN for local SARL is the matricule number assigned by the RCS/LBR and is used for direct tax filings. The application must be accompanied by supporting documentation evidencing the intended taxable activity in Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. Resident SARLs are default entity-level taxpayers subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax. Available statutory elections include Luxembourg VAT grouping (assujetti unique under Article 63 L.L.T.V.A.) and corporate income tax group relief under Article 164bis LIR for resident companies forming a 95% owned fiscal unity. Hybrid mismatch rules under the EU ATAD are mandatorily applied; no elective hybrid mismatch treatment is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 net annual turnover (small business exemption threshold); non-established taxable persons have no general turnover threshold and must register if Luxembourg VAT becomes chargeable, subject to the EU OSS, reverse charge and distance sales rules
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime applies to standard B2B transactions in Luxembourg. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for suppliers to the Luxembourg public sector through Peppol-BIS / Factur-X. Electronic invoices must conform to EU VAT invoicing authenticity rules and may be exchanged via any technology that guarantees chain of custody. There is no mandatory API-based continuous transaction control tax 'clearance' in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A taxable export of goods produced in Luxembourg, including surgical suture needle assemblies, is eligible for the 0% VAT rate under Article 56 L.L.T.V.A. when the goods are physically shipped or transported to a destination outside the European Union by the supplier, the customer or a third party acting on their behalf, and the goods leave the EU no later than three months after the supply. The exporter must retain conclusive and consistent documentary evidence proving the actual departure from the EU, the identity of the acquirer and the price paid. Offshore services directly linked to exported goods (e.g. freight, handling and ancillary logistics) may also qualify for zero rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/DAU) bearing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and export date
Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, CIM railway consignment note or air waybill evidencing physical departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice annotated with the legal zero-rating reference (Article 56 L.L.T.V.A.)
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT / bank credit confirmation showing settlement of the export sale
Evidence of the non-EU customer identity and destination customs status, including delivery note and transport insurance certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg tax authorities closely scrutinise export zero-rating claims and may deny the 0% rate and reassess VAT at 17% where the export movement cannot be objectively substantiated. Penalties include late-payment interest, an additional tax surcharge of up to twice the tax evaded, criminal fines up to EUR 25,000, retrospective clawback of input VAT recovered under false export declarations, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud under Article 80 L.L.T.V.A. The standard five-year limitation period permits retrospective assessments and recovery of under-declared VAT attributable to unjustified export zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem; supervisory authority for macro/micro-prudential and monetary operations is the BCL, while the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises banks, payment institutions, and e-money institutions. The Luxembourg Ministry of Finance sets legislative policy, but for foreign exchange control there is no general licensing authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has full currency convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. As a euro-area member, the euro is the lawful currency. Intra-EU capital movements, payments, and profit repatriation are fully liberalised under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU Capital Movement Directive (Directive 88/361/EEC). No authorisation or central bank notification is required for profit remittances, dividend declarations, interest, royalties, or repayment of intra-group loans, subject only to general AML/KYC documentary thresholds, withholding tax obligations, and the EU Anti-Money Laundering framework. Non-euro receipts may be converted freely at market rates. The practical hurdle is not convertibility but corporate documentation and beneficial ownership transparency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender rules, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed timeline for repatriation of export receipts in Luxembourg or the wider euro area. Exporters may maintain foreign-currency accounts indefinitely, provided that such accounts are declared within the BCL's external statistics reports (Collection, reporting of balance of payments and international investment position) when threshold triggers are met. A surgical suture manufacturer receiving USD export proceeds from the United States or elsewhere may hold, sweep, or convert those proceeds without FX surrender; however, for AML and treasury efficiency, the company should adopt a cash concentration policy and record a monthly FX remittance forecast.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with significant legal caveats. Luxembourg allows passporting of EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions under PSD2, subject to authorisation by either the CSSF or the home-state authority. For a manufacturing SARL requiring trade settlement via SWIFT MT103 and documentary letters of credit, digital EMIs such as Belvian, Mangopay, or cross-border EMI licences in Lithuania, Ireland, or the Netherlands can technically open virtual IBANs and offer FX. However, they are not suitable substitutes for a Tier-1 domestic bank because (i) most EMIs do not provide letter of credit issuance or discounting, (ii) underwriting is frequently algorithmically risk-averse to medical manufacturing and interposed holding structures, and (iii) a euro-area operating company should maintain an account at a CSSF-supervised credit institution to obtain robust bank reference letters for VAT, trade, and future fundraising. Offshore fintech EMIs in third countries are legally disfavoured for treasury clearing and are unlikely to meet the standards of Luxembourg's bank reference requirements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: As a rule under Luxembourg AML law (Loi du 12 novembre 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02), credit institutions must identify and verify the identity of clients and their beneficial owners. In practice, for non-resident directors or individuals not previously known to the bank, a physical presence for a KYC interview is mandatory at onboarding. Luxembourg Tier-1 banks are increasingly using video-identification and eIDAS certificates for remote onboarding, but for a newly formed SARL with capital escrow needs, banks generally require at least one in-person meeting with the authorized manager and a notarised deed. A statutory right to remote account opening does not exist; each bank applies CSSF 17/650 digital onboarding guidelines. Therefore the blueprint must budget for a physical visit to Luxembourg by the manager and treasury signatory, or use a delegated authorised representative (duly authorised by Power of Attorney).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) situated in a high-risk third country or having a medium-to-high adverse media profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent negative-news screening report, passport and residence proof, source-of-wealth statement, confirmation of no adverse regulatory action, EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening result, and a sworn declaration of provenance of funds for capital subscription.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-layered ownership structure involving a Panama, Delaware, or non-transparent intermediate holding entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete organisational chart with percentage holdings, official registry extracts for each layer, written confirmation of economic substance, annual accounts or opening balance sheet of each vehicle, tax residence certificates, and a memorandum explaining the commercial/regional treasury purpose of the intermediate entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share capital contribution materially exceeding the mandatory €12,000 minimum for a SARL and arriving from a foreign jurisdiction with a large one-time wire.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original capital contribution agreement, notarial deed or private deed with evidence of bank confirmation, source-of-funds documents (bank statements, contract of sale, inheritance certificate, or investor audited accounts), and a board resolution authorising the capital increase, together with a funds-flow schematic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient local substance: no national identifier, registered office, or payroll records in Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execution copy of the lease agreement or notarised sub-lease for the registered office, certificate of domiciliation by an approved Luxembourg trust company, VAT number and EU VAT certificate (TVA/LT), social security registration certificates, photographs of premises, employment declarations and copies of employment contracts of local staff, and an annual external substance declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Surgical suture manufacturing requires statutory licence and the bank requests proof of regulatory compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Ministry of Health import/export and manufacturing operational notification, Class IIa/Class IIb medical device CE certificate under Regulation (EU) 2017/745, ISO 13485 certificate, Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) evidence, completed due diligence checklist on raw-material traceability and sterility protocols, and a copy of all valid authorisations from the Ministry of Health or competent notified body.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the initial share capital injection and subsequent capital increases of the LU_SARL, the share subscription amount must be wired to the bank account of the notary or the SARL's designated euro capital escrow account before incorporation. The wire shall be executed by SWIFT MT103 with a precise remittance information field (field 70) referencing: 'SUBSCRIPTION AGREEMENT [date] – SHAREHOLDERS [name(s)] – SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – NOTARY REPERTOIRE NUMBER'. Beneficiary bank should be the domestic Tier-1 lender selected for escrow. For shareholder loans or intercompany route funding originating from related parties, the routing must be clearly labelled as a loan disbursement and preferably be structured by written loan agreement to confirm arm's-length terms; however, no Luxembourg foreign exchange approval is required. The bank will execute AML source-of-funds verification, obtain a 'BLOCKING CONFIRMATION' (attestation de blocage de fonds), and release funds only after the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) filing. For all external assets and liabilities above €500,000 or outstanding threshold, the SARL must file a BCL balance-of-payments statistical report (reporting scheme of BCL Direct Investment and Financial Assets/Liabilities) through its bank. Inbound currency other than euro must be converted on the same day into EUR through the bank's treasury, using BCL reference rates or permitted daily market fix, and the conversion confirmation must be archived.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for surgical suture trade disbursements shall be SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for advance payments, open-account settlements, and distributor payments, and SWIFT MT700/MT720 irrevocable documentary letters of credit for confirmed purchase orders, especially from public hospital tenders and government distributors. The beneficiary of inbound LCs may be the LU_SARL, but in high-risk markets the SARL should advise LCs through Luxembourg Tier-1 bank and request confirmation by a top-25 global bank if sovereign risk or LC-issuing bank risk is elevated. For payments related to raw material imports (polyglycolic acid, polymer needles, packaging, sterilization services), the SARL shall use MT103/TT wire transfer with e-invoicing consistency; for capital equipment imports, an unconfirmed or confirmed L/C at sight is appropriate. All SWIFT messages must include the correct ISO 20022 purpose codes: 'TRPT' (payment of trade), 'CAPT' (capital transfer), 'GDST' (goods trade), 'INTC' (intra-group financial transactions) or 'TREA' (treasury operations) as applicable, plus a full reference to the SEPA direct debit/creditor identifier and VAT number to facilitate customs and VAT clearance. The holding of foreign-currency operating accounts at the Tier-1 bank will allow natural matching of USD/CHF receipts to raw material disbursements; surplus conversion can be executed by the bank’s automatic sweep module. Intra-EU disbursements under €100,000 may be executed via SEPA Instant to reduce clearing time, but documentary LC transactions require traditional SWIFT rails.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX outright forward contract (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) with non-delivery option
FX swap (swap of principal and interest, or spot-forward swap)
Cross-currency interest rate swap (CCIRS) for long-term shareholder loans
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) referencing a convertible offshore currency, if the underlying invoice currency is not freely deliverable in Luxembourg
Vanilla FX options (European put/call on EUR/USD)
Exchange-traded currency futures and options on regulated EU/EEA exchanges

Accumulator and participation forwards, provided the bank's product governance assessment confirms appropriateness for the SARL and the instruments are classified as eligible 'treasury hedging' under MiFID II

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return (corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 28 February of the year following the tax year for calendar-year accounts; within 5 months after the balance sheet date for non-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing assessment, late-payment interest at 10% per annum, penalty of up to 10% of the tax due, and possible daily penalty up to EUR 25 per day for continued default under the General Tax Law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts deposit (balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, notes, and management report when required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), RESA publication service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 7 months after the financial year end (e.g., 31 July 2026 for accounts closing on 31 December 2025)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court summons and coercive fine (astreinte), fine up to EUR 5,000 and further daily penalties for non-compliance; persistent failure may trigger commercial-court strike-off and compulsory liquidation proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (annual beneficial owner data reconfirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (UBO module)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months from the initial or last UBO filing; ownership changes must be filed within 1 month of the relevant share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines between EUR 125 and EUR 1,250 for missing or incomplete filings; knowingly false declarations are subject to criminal fines up to EUR 5,000 and/or imprisonment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory where the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: (i) balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000; (ii) net turnover above EUR 8,800,000; (iii) average workforce above 50 employees. Audit also applies to a company with listed instruments, a credit/financial institution, insurance undertaking, or holding company under supervised financial-sector status.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the Law of 19 December 2002 on statutory accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS is accepted for consolidated accounts and may be elected for unlisted company annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must submit an annual confirmation through the RCS UBO module at least once every 12 months. Any shareholding transfer resulting in a change of ultimate beneficial ownership must be notified within 1 month; where no change has occurred, a nil confirmation stating that the registered beneficial ownership details remain accurate must still be filed annually.
